(a) Redesignation.—The Ellis Island Library on the third floor of the Ellis Island Immigration Museum, located on Ellis Island in New York Harbor, shall be known and redesignated as the “Bob Hope Memorial Library”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the Ellis Island Library on the third floor of the Ellis Island Immigration Museum referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Bob Hope Memorial Library”.

fable.w: This section only renames a library on Ellis Island and directs that references in federal records be read to use the new name. The one tempting cue is the word "regulation" in subsection (b), but that refers to existing records and does not authorize rulemaking or any process. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge a federal decision.
fable.s: shall be known and redesignated as the “Bob Hope Memorial Library”

qwen_block.w: This section simply changes the name of a federal facility. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements to consult with states, tribes, or the public mentioned in the text.
